what_this_is: The list of things Zeta is expected to match. One item per decision, each with a check that runs on its own machine. Drift is not a fault, it is a question: apply, or answer why not.

conventions.unknown_means: the check could not run or could not be read. Never read unknown as aligned.

variables.REPO: the clone this file sits in (sync/..)

items.title: The model is the one we chose, in the config, not the harness default
items.why: A default model changes under you on an upgrade. The pin is what makes a run reproducible.
items.fix: Set model.default (and model.provider) in ~/.hermes/config.yaml. Ours is deepseek-flash on the deepseek provider.

items.title: Hooks run without a prompt
items.why: The gateway, desktop app and cron never answer a first-use prompt, so without this every hook is silently skipped with one log line.

items.title: Concurrent sessions are coordinated, not just co-resident
items.why: Hermes has no cross-session awareness: two sessions editing one repo means last writer wins and nobody notices. peerctl is the guard, wired as four hooks.
items.fix: Install peerctl.py and wire it to on_session_start, pre_llm_call, pre_tool_call (matcher write_file|patch|terminal, fail_closed: false) and on_session_finalize. Design: design/implementations/elio-2026-11-09-concurrent-sessions.md.

items.title: The memory store has contracted records, and the index knows it
items.why: A record whose contract did not parse indexes, searches and reads fine while being classified as substrate, so the failure is silent.

check.sh: test -f "$HERMES_HOME/data/kb/kb.sqlite3" && sqlite3 "$HERMES_HOME/data/kb/kb.sqlite3" "select count(*) from scope where evidence='contracted';"

items.fix: Frontmatter contract at the top level (namespace, volatility, epistemic, origin, evidence), then reindex. Shape: spec/ in this repo.

items.title: Retrieval runs before the answer, not after the apology
items.why: Measured failure: a record that was the top search hit was answered "I don't remember", because no search ran. A prompt line is a nudge; a hook is a gate.
items.fix: Wire a pre_llm_call hook that searches the contracted records for the user's message, and a post_llm_call observer that records disclaimers. Both in one script is fine.

items.title: The board log passes its own verifier
items.why: Two independent readings of one format is the only useful test of it, and verify is the cheap one. A board that reads clean but verifies dirty is two boards.

check.sh: test -d "$BOARD_LOG" && cd "$BOARD_LOG" && python3 board/board.py verify >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo ok

items.fix: Run `python3 board/board.py verify` and read the line it complains about; ids and prefixes must match the file they sit in.

items.title: Something is actually polling the board, and it says so
items.why: A cursor only moves when a message exists, so a healthy watcher on a quiet board and a wedged one look identical. The heartbeat is the only difference. Thirty minutes rather than fifteen: a boundary wide enough to survive one missed poll and a restart, and a drift line that still means the poller has stopped.
items.fix: Run the delivery watcher on a timer or a supervised unit and touch a heartbeat after every completed poll, not after every successful one.

items.title: At least one scheduled job is gated by a monitor script
items.why: A job that wakes the model on a schedule pays for a turn whether or not anything changed. A monitor script makes a quiet period cost nothing.

check.sh: test -f "$HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json" && python3 -c "import json,sys;d=json.load(open('$HERMES_HOME/cron/jobs.json'));rows=d if isinstance(d,list) else d.get('jobs',[]);print(sum(1 for r in rows if r.get('monitor_script')))"

items.fix: Give the job a monitor_script that prints nothing when there is nothing to do; the scheduler then skips the model call.

items.title: Anything published has auth in front of it
items.why: The dashboard and the human channel are reachable from a phone away from home. Tailnet membership is not authentication.
items.fix: Set dashboard.basic_auth with a password hash (never a plaintext password), or do not publish the port.

items.title: The disk has room for the archive to grow
items.why: Every backup, index and session store fails in a way that is hard to read once the disk is full.
items.fix: Free space, or move the archive. Value is GiB free on the volume holding $HOME.
